one_liner: Jomo Kenyatta became the first president of the Republic of Kenya.
title: Jomo Kenyatta becomes Kenya's first president

one_liner: Pennsylvania becomes the second state to ratify the US Constitution.
title: Pennsylvania is second to ratify the US Constitution

one_liner: The Plymouth Colony establishes the system of trial by 12-men jury in the American colonies.
title: Plymouth Colony establishes trial by jury

one_liner: The Massachusetts Bay Colony organizes three militia regiments to defend the colony against the Pequot Indians, a date now considered the founding of the National Guard of the United States.
title: Massachusetts Bay Colony organizes three militia regiments

one_liner: Dartmouth College (campus pictured) was established by royal charter in present-day Hanover, New Hampshire.
title: Dartmouth College is founded by royal charter

one_liner: The Glasgow Underground Railway is opened by the Glasgow District Subway Company.
title: The Glasgow Underground Railway opens

one_liner: Upon completing the third extra-vehicular activity of Apollo 17, American astronaut Gene Cernan became the last person to date to walk on the Moon.
title: Gene Cernan becomes the last person to walk on the Moon

one_liner: Giacomo Puccini's comic opera Gianni Schicchi premiered at the Metropolitan Opera in New York City.
title: Puccini's Gianni Schicchi premieres at the Met

one_liner: Symphony No. 9 ("From the New World" a.k.a. the "New World Symphony") by Antonín Dvořák premieres in a public afternoon rehearsal at Carnegie Hall in New York City, followed by a concert premiere on the evening of December 16.
title: Dvořák's New World Symphony premieres at Carnegie Hall

one_liner: Sixteen-year-old Ella Stewart sent the first telegraphed message from Arizona Territory.
title: Ella Stewart sends Arizona Territory's first telegram

one_liner: Constantine VIII (depicted) became the sole Byzantine emperor, 63 years after being crowned co-emperor.
title: Constantine VIII becomes sole Byzantine emperor

one_liner: Czech composer Antonín Dvořák's New World Symphony (audio featured) premiered at Carnegie Hall in New York City.
title: Dvořák's New World Symphony debuts in New York

one_liner: Settlers of the Canterbury Association aboard Randolph and Charlotte Jane arrived to establish a colony at Christchurch, New Zealand.
title: Canterbury settlers arrive to found Christchurch

one_liner: Wales and England played the first match of what became rugby’s Six Nations Championship.
title: Wales hosts the first Home Nations rugby fixture

one_liner: Near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first controlled, powered, heavier-than-air human flight.
title: The Wright brothers make the first powered flight

one_liner: SpaceShipOne, piloted by Brian Binnie, makes its first powered and first supersonic flight.
title: SpaceShipOne makes its first supersonic flight

one_liner: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania's Schenley Park Casino, which was the first multi-purpose arena with the technology to create an artificial ice surface in North America, is destroyed in a fire.
title: Fire destroys Pittsburgh's Schenley Park Casino

one_liner: The national anthem of the Russian Empire, "God Save the Tsar!", is first performed.
title: God Save the Tsar! is performed for the first time

one_liner: In Angola, New York, the last coach of a Lake Shore Railway train derailed, plunged 40 feet (12 m) down a gully, and caught fire, resulting in approximately 49 deaths.
title: A Lake Shore train derails at Angola, killing 49

one_liner: New Jersey becomes the third state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.
title: New Jersey is third to ratify the U.S. Constitution

one_liner: Thomas Paine published the first in a series of pamphlets entitled The American Crisis, opening with the line: "These are the times that try men's souls."
title: Thomas Paine publishes the first American Crisis pamphlet

one_liner: Titanic, the fourth-highest-grossing film of all time with a worldwide total of more than US$2.2 billion, was released in the United States.
title: Titanic is released in the United States

one_liner: A Christmas Carol (illustration pictured), a novella by Charles Dickens about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge and his transformation after being visited by ghosts, was published.
title: Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol

one_liner: The Louisiana Purchase is completed at a ceremony in New Orleans.
title: The Louisiana Purchase is completed in New Orleans

one_liner: South Carolina becomes the first state to attempt to secede from the United States with the South Carolina Declaration of Secession.
title: South Carolina is first to declare secession

one_liner: Experimental Breeder Reactor I near Arco, Idaho, U.S., became the world's first electricity-generating nuclear power plant when it became able to illuminate four 200-watt light bulbs.
title: EBR-I becomes the first nuclear plant to make electricity

one_liner: Settlers from the United States in Mexican Texas made the first attempt to secede from Mexico, establishing the short-lived Republic of Fredonia.
title: Texas settlers declare the Republic of Fredonia

one_liner: The Pilgrims aboard the Mayflower landed at present-day Plymouth, Massachusetts, to establish the Plymouth Colony.
title: The Mayflower Pilgrims land at Plymouth

one_liner: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first full-length cel-animated feature in film history, premiered at the Carthay Circle Theatre in Los Angeles.
title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premieres in Los Angeles

one_liner: A dike ruptured at a waste containment area for a coal-fired power plant in Kingston, Tennessee, releasing 1.1 billion gallons (4.2 million m3) of coal fly ash slurry (aftermath pictured) in the largest industrial spill in US history.
title: Kingston coal ash spill is the largest in US history

one_liner: Sino-Burmese War: The war ends with the Qing dynasty withdrawing from Burma forever.
title: The war ends with the Qing dynasty withdrawing from Burma forever.

one_liner: Pope Innocent I began his papacy, succeeding Anastasius I.
title: Pope Innocent I begins his papacy

one_liner: Jane Austen's novel Emma was first published, the last novel released during her lifetime.
title: Jane Austen's novel Emma is published

one_liner: Moscow State Academy of Choreography is founded under the reign of Catherine II. It is the second ballet school in Russia after Vaganova Academy of Russian Ballet.
title: The Moscow State Academy of Choreography is founded

one_liner: The first film adaptation of Väinö Linna's novel The Unknown Soldier, directed by Edvin Laine, premieres
title: First film adaptation of The Unknown Soldier premieres

one_liner: Aida, one of Giuseppe Verdi's most popular operas, made its debut in Cairo, Egypt.
title: Verdi's Aida premieres in Cairo

one_liner: The opera Aida premieres in Cairo, Egypt.
title: The opera Aida premieres in Cairo

one_liner: The United Kingdom and the United States signed a peace treaty in Ghent, present-day Belgium, ending the War of 1812.
title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812

one_liner: Isaac Newton, English physicist and mathematician.
title: Isaac Newton is born

one_liner: Wagner's Siegfried Idyll is first performed.
title: Wagner's Siegfried Idyll receives its first performance

one_liner: American physician Ephraim McDowell performed the world's first removal of an ovarian tumor.
title: Ephraim McDowell performs the first ovarian tumor removal

one_liner: Thespis, the first comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, premiered at the Gaiety Theatre in London.
title: Gilbert and Sullivan's first opera Thespis premieres

one_liner: Philip Gidley King, Governor of New South Wales, ordered the formation of the Governor's Body Guard of Light Horse, described as the first full-time military unit raised in Australia.
title: Australia's first full-time military unit is formed

one_liner: The opera Agrippina, described as George Frideric Handel's first masterpiece, premiered in Venice.
title: Handel's opera Agrippina premieres in Venice

one_liner: HMS Beagle departed Plymouth, England, on a voyage to South America that established Charles Darwin (pictured) as a naturalist.
title: HMS Beagle departs Plymouth for South America

one_liner: A period of unrest in Wittenberg following the arrival of three men of the Radical Reformation, known as the Zwickau prophets, was quelled after Martin Luther's release from custody.
title: Wittenberg unrest is quelled after Luther's release

one_liner: The reconstructed Hagia Sophia in Constantinople was inaugurated; built as a church, it later became a mosque and a museum.
title: The Hagia Sophia is inaugurated in Constantinople

one_liner: Galileo Galilei became the first person to observe the planet Neptune (pictured), although he mistakenly catalogued it as a fixed star.
title: Galileo observes Neptune, mistaking it for a star

one_liner: South Australia and Adelaide are founded.
title: South Australia and the city of Adelaide are founded

one_liner: Westminster Abbey, built by Edward the Confessor as the first Romanesque church in England, was first consecrated.
title: Westminster Abbey is first consecrated

one_liner: The launch of HMS Warrior, with her combination of screw propeller, iron hull and iron armour, renders all previous warships obsolete.
title: HMS Warrior's launch renders older warships obsolete

one_liner: To counter the French Navy's Gloire, the world's first ironclad warship, the Royal Navy launched HMS Warrior, the world's first iron-hulled armoured warship.
title: The Royal Navy launches HMS Warrior, an iron-hulled warship

one_liner: Cecil B. DeMille begins filming Hollywood's first feature film, The Squaw Man
title: Cecil B. DeMille Starts Filming Hollywood's First Feature Film

one_liner: Canadian ice hockey player Ernie McLea scores the first hat-trick in Stanley Cup play, and the Cup-winning goal as the Montreal Victorias defeat the Winnipeg Victorias 6–5.
title: Ernie McLea scores the first Stanley Cup hat-trick

one_liner: The Discovery Expedition under Robert Falcon Scott attained a new Farthest South point in Antarctica.
title: Scott's Discovery Expedition reaches a new Farthest South

one_liner: The University of Galway, University College Cork and Queen's University Belfast were established as part of the Queen's University of Ireland.
title: Galway, Cork and Belfast colleges are established

one_liner: Byzantine general Belisarius completes the conquest of Sicily, defeating the Gothic garrison of Palermo (Panormos), and ending his consulship for the year.
title: Belisarius completes his conquest of Sicily

one_liner: The first Huguenots set sail from France to the Cape of Good Hope.
title: The first Huguenots sail from France for the Cape of Good Hope

one_liner: Romanian Television begins live black-and-white broadcasts on New Year's Eve in Bucharest.
title: Romanian Television Begins Broadcasting
